additional_requirements: Functioning is not markedly impaired apart from the impact of the delusion(s) or its ramifications

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

symptom.disease_info: Delusional Disorder is characterized by the presence of one or more persistent delusions lasting at least one month, in the absence of prominent hallucinations, disorganized thought, or marked negative symptoms seen in schizophrenia. Outside of the impact of the delusional beliefs, functioning is often relatively preserved, and behavior may not appear obviously odd or bizarre to casual observers. The content of the delusions is typically non‑bizarre or only mildly implausible (e.g., being conspired against, deceived by a partner, or having a hidden illness), and mood symptoms, if present, are usually secondary and not pervasive. It is distinguished from psychotic disorders such as schizophrenia by the lack of significant cognitive disorganization and from mood disorders with psychotic features by the independence of the delusions from mood episodes, with a course that can be chronic and insidiously progressive.

patient.stressor: Roughly two years ago, after a period of increased travel and late nights related to a store remodel, Cassidy and her spouse had several tense arguments about time together and social boundaries. Around this time, Cassidy began to focus intensely on small, ordinary behaviors—her spouse checking their phone, changing passwords, or being quiet after work—as signs of a hidden agenda, gradually building a fixed narrative that her partner and even some friends were secretly exchanging information about her and testing her loyalty. Over the ensuing 1 year and 9 months, she remained high‑energy at work but grew more suspicious in her marriage, insisting on interpreting casual comments and social media posts as coded messages, which led to repeated conflicts about trust and privacy despite the absence of any confirming evidence. Her spouse eventually suggested counseling, and when couples therapy stalled because Cassidy could not let go of these ideas, the therapist recommended an individual psychiatric evaluation to better understand the fixed beliefs that were driving the relationship strain.
patient.chief_complaint: “I can’t shake the belief that my spouse and friends have been secretly plotting behind my back, no matter how much they deny it.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: Even when my spouse shows me their messages or my friends swear nothing weird is going on, I still feel absolutely sure they’ve got some group chat or code words they use online and in person to talk about me and see how I react, like I’m being tested all the time and nobody will just admit it.

add_requirements.Functioning is not markedly impaired apa: Outside of all this suspicion about my spouse and friends, I still run my store smoothly, keep up with my staff, and handle my day-to-day responsibilities without any real problems.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: The main way this affects me is in my marriage and close friendships, because I keep bringing up these concerns and checking for secret signs, which leads to more arguments and distance even though everything else in my life is running fine.
add_requirements.duration: These beliefs about my spouse and friends secretly plotting have been going on for about a year and nine months, ever since that big store remodel when I was traveling more and we were arguing about time together.
